issues.failure_explanation: For the oracle actually used in Algorithm 4, the noise is \xi_{t+1}(s)=v_t(\tilde s)-(Pv_t)(s), so \|\xi_{t+1}\|_\infty\le 2\|v_t\|_\infty and E[\|\xi_{t+1}\|_\infty^2|F_t]\le 4\|v_t\|_\infty^2, which is iterate-dependent and not bounded by any deterministic \sigma^2 a priori (the crude a.s. bound \|v_{t+1}\|_\infty\le 2(\|v_t\|_\infty+\alpha_t R) grows geometrically). The stability lemmas (lem:projSA_stability_template, lem:optionB_stability, lem:contract_noise_bounded_iterates) assume the uniform bound \sigma^2 and use it to conclude that the iterates are bounded in second moment; but bounded iterates are exactly what would be needed to justify a uniform \sigma^2. Theorem thm:main_sa_rate and its formal version thm:projSA_rate_template therefore rest on a hypothesis that is never verified for the algorithm they analyze, and the main-text statement does not even list it as a hypothesis.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the uniform bound by the state-dependent bound E[\|\xi_{t+1}\|_\infty^2|F_t]\le 4\|v_t\|_\infty^2\le C(1+\|e_t\|_q^2), carry the extra \alpha_t^2 C m_t term through the moment recursion m_{t+1}\le[(1-\alpha_t(1-\hat\gamma))^2+C'\alpha_t^2]m_t+C''\alpha_t^2 (which still yields sup_t m_t<\infty and the same T^{-1/2} rate since \sum\alpha_t^2<\infty), and then define \sigma^2 in terms of the resulting bound B_{\sup}^2; restate the theorems accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The O(T^{-1/2}) convergence guarantee for Algorithm 4, the resulting end-to-end query complexity, and the residual-estimation bound (which uses B_v^2=E\|v\|_\infty^2 and E\|v_T-v^\star\|_\infty) are established only under an unverified assumption; as written they do not apply to the algorithm with the paper's own generative-model oracle.
issues.title: Uniform oracle second-moment bound is assumed but is not satisfied a priori by the paper's own sampled operator, whose noise scales with the (unbounded, random) iterate
issues.why_classification: The rate and method survive, but closing the gap requires a genuine (if standard) additional argument for iterate-dependent noise and a restatement of constants across several lemmas and theorems; it is not a one-line local fix, yet no result is lost.
